checks: An extreme source base forces its row onto that same base. A base-zero row has endpoint probabilities q and q by its base mean. The common normal and physical mean imply q(2h_0-h_--h_+)=0. When q is positive, every paired midpoint lies in the actual middle exposed face by the body inclusion and equality of the support heights.

Weighting the old probability pairing by q yields marginals gamma_- and gamma_+, including their normal marks, and replacing both old branches by twice the paired midpoint preserves the entire physical mean and row mass. The retained base-zero targets have full marginal eta_0 because endpoint sources cannot feed them. Jensen disintegrates to the first conditional convex order by countably many determining tests. The old tuple law also disintegrates relative to lambda and provides the coupling required by the pointwise selection theorem.

Normal preservation and the original target marginal give (u)_#nu=lambda. Hence the unnormalized conditional source and all target, crossflow, tuple and midpoint kernels have mass at most one. They are supported on fixed compact sets. Kernel domination follows from joint domination by comparing a countable determining family against all Borel normal restrictions. The two conditional crossflow masses coincide and vanish off the tight set on one common full Borel set.

Positive common crossflow mass ensures positive endpoint surface kernels. The all-ball predecessor ensures the middle surface kernel has positive mass. The full surface kernels, including the middle one, are equivalent to intrinsic face measure. In common dimension zero each kernel is an atom. The ball inequality bounds the smaller endpoint atom mass by the middle atom mass, while the crossflow is at most that smaller mass. The unique midpoint coupling already meets the ceiling. If the common crossflow mass is zero, the old midpoint and the new tuple kernel are zero.

In common positive dimension, take the full endpoint faces as compact chart supports. Endpoint densities extended by zero outside their good sets represent their respective full surface measures. The middle upper density restricted to the compact midpoint set is Borel, integrable, and agrees almost everywhere there with the actual middle conditional surface density. The all-good-pairs bound is exactly the variable-density hypothesis at weights one half. The output chart maps affinely and isometrically to the base-zero physical plane, so comparison there implies comparison for each finite ambient physical convex function and transports the domination to the actual middle kernel.

Pointwise chart choices serve only to prove feasibility. The accepted Borel selector operates with fixed compact supports and original physical coordinates, on the Borel full normal set where the endpoint masses agree. The joint ceiling follows by integration in u, and all selected tuple components are in the actual exposed endpoint faces almost everywhere by their marginals.

Tagged reconstruction applies to both established convex orders. Its Borel intermediate split produces an augmented tuple branch with integrated marginal twice the selected tuple law. Disintegrating that augmented branch over the physical marked source gives a finite Borel row kernel. The equal endpoint probabilities make one half of this row kernel the weighted pairing of its two final branches. Normalizing by its row mass where positive gives the probability pairing, and its integrated midpoint law is exactly rho.

All base-zero source rows together send their base-zero branch to eta_0 and their endpoint branches to the exact original physical crossflows. Keeping the original endpoint-source rows restores the residual endpoint marginals eta_z minus gamma_z. The tagged reconstruction keeps the marked source marginal and preserves the physical mean and normal. For every closed affine halfspace, a midpoint in the halfspace requires at least one endpoint in it, with the same pointwise comparison and tuple law for all halfspaces.

Apply it on the common full Borel normal set described in the proof, and extend the selected kernel by zero if a version on the whole sphere is desired.
